source.title: Junior School Curriculum Design — Pre-Technical Studies Grade 7 (First published 2022, Revised 2024)
source.notes: Read directly and in full via the Read tool (no pages param) per CURRICULUM-MINING-GUIDE.md. All 5 strands / 13 sub-strands read from the 'SUMMARY OF STRANDS AND SUB STRANDS' table (p.vii) and cross-checked against each strand's detailed section (pp.1-31) plus Appendix 2 (learning resources / non-formal activities, pp.34-42).

subStrands.name: 3.2 Metallic Materials
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify types of metallic materials used in a work environment
Describe the physical properties of metallic materials found in a work environment
Relate metallic materials to their use in a work environment
Appreciate the use of metallic materials in production
keyInquiryQuestions: Why are metallic materials important in day-to-day life?
learningExperiences: Search for information on metallic materials
Prepare a checklist for identifying types of metallic materials (steel, aluminum, copper)
Perform practical activities to examine the physical properties of metallic materials (magnetism, conductivity of heat and electricity, appearance)
Discuss the physical properties of metallic materials
Match metallic materials to their use in the work environment
linkedLearningAreas: Integrated Science — exploring types of metals
scopeNotes: include: the metal pool is exactly steel, aluminium, copper — the design does not name any other metallic material for this sub-strand, so the pool is a genuine hard floor AND ceiling, unlike SI.3's SI units where the source names more than got shipped.

include: exactly four physical properties are named — magnetism, conductivity of heat, conductivity of electricity, appearance. Rust/corrosion behaviour is not explicitly named here but is standard, well-known descriptive content for these three metals and was already present in the pre-existing skill (aluminium 'resistant to rusting') — kept as a defensible enrichment, not a curriculum stretch.
subStrands.assessmentSignal: 3.0 strand rubric (shared across 3.1-3.3): top band identifies types 'giving examples for each type', describes properties 'citing examples', and relates materials to use 'for all materials' — recall alone (no examples/application) caps at the second-from-top band.
subStrands.notes: Audited 2026-08-15 after user feedback that web/src/skills/preTechnicalG7/metallicMaterials.ts felt repetitive — same 3-metal recall facts recurring 4+ times per 20-question session. Root cause was NOT missing curriculum content (the pool of 3 metals / 4 properties is exactly what KICD specifies) but too few distinct facts, scenarios and question branches drawing on that pool, plus one fully static (non-randomized) fill-blank branch. Fixed by: expanding PROPERTY_FACTS from 9 to 15 entries, adding 9 Kenyan-localized rng-varied Apply-tier reasoning scenarios and 3 Evaluate-tier trade-off scenarios (copper-vs-aluminium power lines, coastal gate material, structural-load steel-vs-aluminium) per RIGOR-STANDARDS.md, adding a real-world-item categorize branch, randomizing the previously-static fill-blank branch across 6 templates, and fixing a real density-ordering bug (METALS.density values didn't match the metal each was assigned to real-world density, so 'ordering' branch grading silently contradicted its own explanation text).
